structured_output.hypothesis: In measured stature of US males by single year of age, annual height increments are largest in infancy, stay moderate and roughly constant through about ages 4-9, rise to a clear pubertal peak in the early teens, and fall to near zero by ages 18-20.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using exam-weighted (WTMEC) mean standing height (recumbent length under age 2) of males by completed year of age, pooled across NHANES cycles, define the annual increment D(a) = mean(a+1) - mean(a) in cm/yr. All four conditions must hold. (1) Infancy: D(0) >= 2.0 x the mean of D(4..9). (2) Steady childhood: for ages 4-9, every D(a) lies within +/-25% of the mean of D(4..9), and that mean is between 4.5 and 7.5 cm/yr. (3) Teen quickening: max D(a) over ages 10-15 >= 1.25 x the mean of D(4..9), and the age of that maximum is 11-15. (4) Arrest: mean of D(18..19) <= 1.0 cm/yr and <= 20% of the mean of D(4..9). Females are analysed the same way as a secondary, non-deciding check, because the claim is about boys and man.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any one of the four pass conditions is not met for males. Examples: D(0) < 2.0 x the childhood mean; any childhood D(a) outside +/-25% of the childhood mean, so there is no near-steady plateau; the teen maximum is < 1.25 x the childhood mean, or occurs outside ages 11-15, so there is no distinct quickening; or D(18..19) > 1.0 cm/yr, so there is no arrest.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'curve of growth for length or stature' is read as population mean stature versus age, and growth rate as the first difference of that mean in cm per year. 'Babyhood' is age 0-1 and 'early boyhood' is ages about 4-9. 'Soon after the boy is in his teens' is ages 11-15. 'Gradual arrest' is ages 18-20. 'Almost steady' is operationalised as +/-25% of the childhood mean, and 'marked quickening' as a >=25% rise over that mean. Modern reinterpretation: NHANES is cross-sectional, so differences between successive age-group means estimate velocity but are not individual longitudinal velocities. They are also blurred by secular trends and by the spread in timing of puberty. Pooling cycles reduces sampling noise.

dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES examiners measure standing height and recumbent length, not self-reports, across the whole age range from birth to adulthood. Download the Body Measures (BMX) and Demographics (DEMO) files for each cycle. Fields used: RIDAGEYR and RIDAGEMN (age), RIAGENDR (sex), BMXHT (standing height, cm), BMXRECUM (recumbent length, cm), and WTMEC2YR (exam weight).
